title: ModelServing rolling update concrete case catalogue

idAllocation.order: Sequential RUN numbering in current taxonomy/body order; DENY rows consume no RUN number.
idAllocation.references: All RUN references in this catalogue and the Markdown table use current IDs. Previous IDs and ID mappings are not retained.
idAllocation.archives: ROLLING_UPDATE_SCENARIOS.md and RUNNER_DESIGN_V1.md remain unchanged and are not authoritative for current case IDs. Existing core-60 YAMLs and Kind evidence keep their IDs.

contract.format: Documentation catalogue, not directly kubectl-applicable YAML or an implemented test runner.
contract.verificationAccounting: Original 684 case records retain their initial 2026-09-05 verification snapshot. counts.verifiedOnBaseline counts only recorded case statuses, not all external runs. RUN-001..RUN-060 have later independent Kind evidence in ../../../kthena-rollout-runner/docs/KIND_RESULTS.md; those fixed-replica runs do not verify the 84 added scaling cases. This update adds no Kind run or result backfill. The four-category reordering changes no recorded execution outcome and adds no Kind verification. The RUN renumbering changes identifiers and references only; all recorded case statuses are unchanged.

scalingDuringRollout.sharedContract: ROLLING_UPDATE_CASE_TABLE.md §A.4; applies only to the 84 added cases

HOLD_READY.readiness: All A/B entry/worker Pods start with the readiness file absent. Runner releases baseline A first and subsequently releases complete logical units by exact Pod UID; only actual Pod Ready grants credit. Never patch Pod.status.

AUTO_READY_INTERLEAVE.readiness: Use the ordinary auto-ready fixture, including new A/B Pods. No runner readiness gating, artificial startup delay, controller pause or finalizer to force overlap.
AUTO_READY_INTERLEAVE.trigger: Observe the specified old replacement start and submit a separate replicas request while the original rollout is demonstrably unfinished. A delayed Watch event alone is not overlap proof.

ATOMIC_SPEC_SCALE.trigger: From a Ready A baseline submit replicas and the B PodSpec in one API request; do not split into two patches.

scalingDuringRollout.rejectionProfile: DENY-094..DENY-097 use controlled in-flight or stable-canary initial states; validate rejection while the previously accepted spec continues to apply.
scalingDuringRollout.observation: Continuous Pod UID/lifecycle/actual Ready/member-layout ledger across all patches, with PodGroup and ControllerRevision auxiliary evidence; ModelServing status is not the availability oracle. Do not assume a global ordering between resource watches.
scalingDuringRollout.dynamicBudgets: Recompute percentages from the stage's desired replicas and inherit observed in-flight deletion commitments. Separate scale-up shortfall, explicitly allowed scale-down and retained-unit replacement; do not apply the fixed-D shortcut mechanically or exempt all deletions during scaling.
scalingDuringRollout.partition: Actual ordinal cutoff; protects future replacement, not a minimum replica count. An already updated B does not revert to A when a new percentage boundary includes it. Do not generally assert final A count equals P.
scalingDuringRollout.finalStabilityStart: After every final/partial-canary predicate, including actual member readiness and cleanup, is first satisfied, not when the spec patch is submitted.
scalingDuringRollout.implementation: Planning only. Not implemented or newly Kind-tested in this catalogue update. Preserve independent case/before/after/intermediate-patch YAMLs when implementing. Missing supported actions => MANUAL_REQUIRED, never PASS.

contract.countUnit: One fixed configuration, initial state and ordered action sequence. Assertions and old analysis references do not add to count. Each row is independent. RUN IDs follow the current taxonomy/body order. Counts at parent and child levels are alternate aggregations, never additional cases.
contract.coverage: Finite boundary and risk-based concrete suite, not the infinite Cartesian product of all integers, Kubernetes PodSpec fields and event interleavings.

schedulingScope.focus: Rolling-update behavior, not scheduler or cluster-topology placement correctness.
schedulingScope.topologyAssertions: Only networkTopology immutability: start with {}, patch to null, assert admission rejection and unchanged stored spec and healthy Pod UIDs. Do not configure actual topology constraints or assert Pod placement.
schedulingScope.excluded: HyperNode/topology-tree construction, dedicated topology labels, topology affinity/anti-affinity and cross-domain placement verification.
schedulingScope.retainedRollingInteractions: Gang and recoveryPolicy combinations; rolling budgets and recovery while new capacity is Pending/NotReady; schedulerName changes checked only for unintended rollout. The scheduling-scope decision adds no cases; RUN renumbering is recorded separately in idAllocation.

contract.sourceRefs: refs are traceability tags in the preserved original analysis, not a claim that every dimension there was fully crossed with every other dimension.
contract.rawConfig: A missing u/s/p key is an omitted request field; numeric zero and null remain distinct inputs. config describes initial settings unless the initial/action column explicitly supplies a valid old spec and a rejected/new submitted spec.
contract.versions: A/B/C differ only in entry/worker container ROLLOUT_VERSION env unless a row explicitly modifies image, readiness, layout, member names or other template fields.
contract.faultPreconditions: Fault-injection rows require isolated Kind plus a reviewed injection mechanism; catalogue does not imply that a hook/error-injection runner already exists.
contract.evidence: Retain raw and server-returned before/after YAML, exact image commit, UID and ordinal timeline, API errors, readiness, deletion state, ControllerRevision Data/owner/references and final status. All rows NOT_RUN_ON_BASELINE.

字段归属与兼容性拒绝

taxonomy.primaryAssignment: Exactly one primary leaf per case. Expected admission rejection belongs to 3; explicit controller/CRD version replacement to 4; injected recovery faults by their primary object to 2; normal flows and dedicated boundary tests otherwise belong to 1 and 3. Auxiliary steps do not create additional counted cases.
taxonomy.caseOrder: Depth-first taxonomy order, matching Markdown body order. RUN IDs are assigned sequentially RUN-001..RUN-671 in this order; DENY IDs remain unchanged. RUN-001..RUN-060 retain their original IDs. Only current case IDs are stored.
taxonomy.groupField: group is the new leaf display name; section and categoryPath identify its hierarchy. legacyGroup and legacyStats preserve the former grouping. Existing subgroup/executionProfile fields retain their previous meaning.
distinctions: Readiness gating for observation is not itself a Pod fault; auto-ready interleaving and atomic replicas+PodSpec updates remain distinct.
Same-image controller restarts and leader failover are recovery tests, not controller upgrades. A post-success restart used only to compare final state does not change the primary classification.
ControllerRevision A/B/C are workload template histories, not controller binary versions.

The former 84 scaling additions are split into 80 runtime cases in 1.2.1 and 4 expected rejections in 3.4.6. Another 35 existing scaling/pre-scale/combined-update cases are in 1.2.1, for 115 runtime cases total.
